---
title: "Should it still fly?"
---

{{< include _model.qmd >}}

```{python}
BUILT_M, SHIFT = 0.016, 0.015

x_np = neutral_point()
x_cg_plan = x_np - 0.10 * c_w
x_cg_built = x_cg_plan + SHIFT

plan = trim(0.01550, x_cg_plan)
built = trim(BUILT_M, x_cg_built)
a_stall, CL_stall = stall(built["V"])

# Pitching moment about the CG, the curve whose zero crossing IS the trim.
# Same shift trim() applies internally: Cm_cg = Cm_ref + CL * (x_cg - x_ref)/c.
a_sweep = np.linspace(0, 14, 141)
Cm_of = lambda x_cg, V: (
    np.array(polars(a_sweep, V=V)["Cm"])
    + np.array(polars(a_sweep, V=V)["CL"]) * (x_cg - x_qc_w) / c_w)
```

::: {.hero}
[`{python} f"{abs(built['alpha']-a_stall):.1f}"`° past the stall]{.hero-value}
[where it trims, against a stall at [`{python} f"{a_stall:.1f}"`°]{.key}]{.hero-label}
:::

**Answer.** Yes, but only just and not well (@fig-asbuilt). Expect it to mush:
nose high, sinking fast, liable to drop a wing. It is not unstable — the
restoring moment is if anything *stronger* than the design's. Stability was never
the problem; where it trims is.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Specified
1. **All-up mass: 16 g** · measured on the built glider by the user, 2026-08-30.
2. **Balance point: 15 mm aft of the plan's** · same measurement · the plan
   called for 149.0 mm aft of the nose, so as built it is at 164.0 mm.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## The static margin disagrees, and it is wrong
It calls this aircraft unstable, because the balance point sits behind the
neutral point. But that neutral point is a straight line fitted across α = 0–8°,
and this glider trims well outside the band — so the label stops describing the
aircraft before the aircraft stops flying. Believe `dCm/dα` at the trim instead:
it needs no neutral point, so it inherits none of the ambiguity in defining one.
:::

```{python}
#| label: fig-asbuilt
#| fig-cap: "Pitching moment about the centre of gravity. Each curve crosses zero where that glider trims, and the shading marks angles beyond the built glider's stall. Both curves slope downwards through their crossing — both aircraft are stable — but the built one trims on the wrong side of the stall."
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 3.4))

for name, t, x_cg, colour in [("as planned", plan, x_cg_plan, "C0"),
                              ("as built", built, x_cg_built, "C3")]:
    ax.plot(a_sweep, Cm_of(x_cg, t["V"]), color=colour, lw=1.8, label=name)
    ax.plot(t["alpha"], 0, "o", color=colour, ms=8, zorder=3)

ax.axvspan(a_stall, 14, color="0.9", zorder=0)
ax.text(a_stall + 0.2, ax.get_ylim()[1] * 0.8, "past the stall",
        fontsize=8, color="0.45")
ax.axhline(0, color="0.3", lw=1)
ax.set_xlabel(r"$\alpha$ [deg]"); ax.set_ylabel(r"$C_m$ about the CG")
ax.set_xlim(0, 14); ax.grid(alpha=0.3); ax.legend()
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
